idea: In lcs.py's inner loop reduce big-int work: compute u = S & m once and use S = (S + u) | (S ^ u) (since S & ~m == S ^ u), dropping the nm dict and its lookup; bind pm.get and loop over a pre-translate
expect: ~5-8% faster (fewer dict lookups and one fewer temporary per iteration), score ~2900+ vs 2748
lesson: The identity S&~m == S^(S&m) doesn't pay off here: replacing the precomputed ~m lookup with an extra XOR on a 60000-bit int costs more than the dict hit it removes (bigint op count, not Python overhead, dominates the inner loop), so the variant ran 11% slower (2246 vs ~1911–2000 baseline).
